subject: Discovery: service guardrails & per-customer policy needs — next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Thompson <eli.thompson@acmehealth.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery: service guardrails & per-customer policy needs — recap

Hi Eli / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has the same view and we can align on next steps. I kept this tight: pain, current stack, success criteria, and immediate asks.

TL;DR: Acme needs per-customer rate limits, tiered quota enforcement, and per-tenant routing rules to ensure critical customers get prioritized throughput during peak windows. You are evaluating both Hosted and Dedicated deployment modes; security & auditability will drive the final decision.

Pain points we heard
- High variability in customer traffic (ML inference spikes tied to batch uploads), causing noisy neighbors and occasional throttling for premium accounts.
- Lack of per-tenant observability: hard to explain SLA misses to customers today.
- Manual workaround for routing premium workloads to dedicated instances -> operational overhead.

Current stack
- In-house inference orchestrator + GKE for orchestration
- Model is a fine-tuned open LLM served via a combination of CPU workers and a small GPU pool
- Authentication + audit logs shipped to Splunk; limited token-level telemetry today

Success criteria (how you’ll evaluate a solution)
- Per-customer SLO shaping: ability to set soft/hard rate limits and quota windows per tenant
- Tiered routing: automated routing to dedicated GPU pools for >X qps customers and graceful fallback to cheaper variants
- Clear cost visibility by tenant (per-token unit economics)
- Security: KMS integration and immutable audit trail for inference requests

Immediate next steps we agreed
1) I’ll send a short design brief summarizing how Redwood implements per-customer quotas, routing policies, and fallback tiers (attached).
2) Eli / Maya to share a representative traffic extract (anonymized) — you mentioned a CSV with 30 days of qps by customer; that helps sizing and policy recommendations.
3) Internal sync: Rachel + Karthik will build a proposed policy template and sizing note and we'll target an internal + customer review next week.

Attachments: redwood-tenant-guardrails-brief.pdf (brief with examples and config snippets).

Questions from our side
- Do you have any hard SLOs already committed for top-tier customers we should be aware of?
- Are there any contractual constraints around routing (e.g., must stay in a single region for some customers)?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the design brief and a short policy template by EOD tomorrow.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

(On attachment: redwood-tenant-guardrails-brief.pdf)
From: Eli Thompson <eli.thompson@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery: service guardrails & per-customer policy needs — recap

Vanessa —

Thanks for the thorough summary; looks accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Top-tier SLO: we have an internal commitment of 95th pctl latency < 400 ms for premium clients during business hours (we report monthly).
- Region constraints: a handful of our customers (mainly in EU) require data residency; for now, US-hosted is fine for the pilot but we'll need a VPC/region plan later.
- Traffic extract: attached is acme-mrp-extract.csv with anonymized tenant ids and qps over the last 30 days.

One ask: can your policy templates represent both burst and sustained quotas (e.g., 1,000 qps burst but sustained 200 qps per tenant), and can we set per-tenant fallback models (quantized variant for cost-sensitive fallback)?

If Redwood can show a config example with a tiered fallback and how billing would look, that will accelerate our procurement folks.

Thanks — Eli

Eli Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
eli.thompson@acmehealth.com | +1 (650) 998-4412

On Tue, Dec 15, 2026 at 02:02 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Eli Thompson <eli.thompson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery: service guardrails & per-customer policy needs — internal + config template draft

Team —

Per Vanessa’s note and Eli’s CSV, I put together a short draft policy template and upload to the shared drive (link below). Highlights:

- Policy model: windows-based quotas + tokenized burst bucket. Example: per-tenant {burst_qps, sustained_qps, daily_quota} with automatic promotion to dedicated routing when sustained_qps > threshold for > 10m.
- Fallback: chainable model variants (full-precision -> 8-bit quantized -> lower-capacity model) with cost delta estimates included.
- Observability: token-level counters exposed into Prometheus and exported to your Splunk instance via our log sink; we include example dashboards.

I also added a short cost table that maps the sample tenants in your CSV to expected monthly inference spend under two rollout options (Hosted + Adaptive Tiering vs Dedicated pools for top N).

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/rd/Acme/guardrails-discovery-notes (redwood policy template v1)

Next actions I propose
1) Vanessa: schedule a 30-min working session with Eli/Maya next week to walk the template and cost table.
2) Karthik: quick sizing note for Dedicated GPU capacity if Acme chooses reserved pools for top 10 tenants.
3) Eli/Maya: confirm a few tenants to include in a small pilot (we recommended 5).

Rachel Kim
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Discovery: service guardrails & per-customer policy needs — internal + config template draft

Thanks Rachel — the template looks useful. We can commit to an initial pilot for 4 tenants: tenant_101, tenant_202, tenant_303, tenant_404 (IDs anonymized in the CSV).

We’d like the pilot to demonstrate:
- Per-tenant sustained quota enforcement with alerts when >90% of daily quota is consumed.
- Automated routing to GPU pool A when sustained_qps exceeds 250 for >10 min.
- Fallback to quantized variant with <15% quality degradation on prompts we’ll provide.

Availability: next Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon PST works for a walk-through. Thanks all — Eli

Eli Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
